title: Activation cadence steward scribble
content:
Purpose and audience
This doc is a rapid working sketch for the activation steward cadence and quick-response run procedures for staged LLM rollouts. Intended audience: release stewards, product owners, SRE oncall, ML infra, and solutions engineering. Not an irrevocable playbook — this is a starting point for a stereo-typed microrelease where latency and quality signals are both first-class.

Top-level goals (short)
- Keep user-visible latency within budget while observing quality regressions (semantic drift, hallucination spikes).
- Fail fast on user-harm signals; fail safely on cost/latency regressions.
- Keep rollback paths short, human-readable, and automatable.

Definitions used here
- Steward: designated person running the activation window (owner of checklist and comms).
- Canary: small traffic slice (user/cohort/feature) that receives the change.
- Exposure window: contiguous timebox during which we hold the canary and observe signals.
- Slice: deterministic partition by user property (region, plan, AB cohort).

Quick cadence (0-day sketch)
1) Pre-activation (T-72 to T-1)
   - T-72: Signal contract agreed (latency P50/P95 targets, quality evaluation pairs, safety flags). List in linked artifacts.
   - T-48: Synthetic smoke tests scheduled against canary routes (LLM prompts + golden answers).
   - T-24: Telemetry queries and dashboards created: latency/err/safety/semantic-regression. Assign oncall and steward.
   - T-4: Preflight run: small traffic replay test (10k requests) under throttled injection to validate billing and autoscaling.
   - T-1: Comms: post in release-ops Slack, email stakeholders with rollback plan and contingency.

2) Activation day (exposure window)
   - Phase A (minutes 0–15): 0.1% traffic for 15 minutes. Steward watches core healthsheet: p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, tail token cost.
   - Phase B (minutes 15–60): 1% traffic for 45 minutes if Phase A green. Run offline evals on sampled responses for semantic drift and safety heuristics.
   - Phase C (hours 1–6): 5% for 2 hours then 10% for 3 hours; ramp further only if both telemetry and sample review are green.
   - Phase D (hours 6–24): held at 25% with automated daily sampling and escalations for the first 24 hours.

Gating checks (automated + human)
- Automated thresholds (fail fast):
  - p95 latency > baseline + 50ms for > 5 consecutive minutes -> automatic rollback trigger.
  - 5xx error rate > 0.5% absolute increase -> automatic rollback.
  - Cost-per-token > baseline * 1.25 for sustained 10 minutes -> throttled revert.
- Manual thresholds (steward evaluates):
  - Safety classifier false-positive/negative delta > 1.5x on sampled set -> steward escalate to safety lead.
  - Semantic drift score (BLEU/ROUGE/Cohere-sim metric) drop beyond agreed delta -> pause ramp and investigate.

Sampling plan and review discipline
- Sampling: store 1% of canary responses (obfuscated) for evaluation; rotate buckets so same accounts are not always sampled.
- Human review: solutions/ML team to review a rotating 20-item set per ramp phase; use checkboxes: hallucination?, offensive?, answer-missing?, acceptable?
- Post-activation audit: 24-hour retrospective entry by steward with: what was observed, what telemetry tripped, and recommended fixes.

Bucketing & cohort selection heuristics
- Prefer deterministic, low-correlation keys (user_id hashed + salt) to avoid correlated exposures.
- Slices to prefer: internal beta users, low-traffic enterprise tenants, small randomized public cohort, mobile-only users.
- Avoid placing high-risk regulated cohorts (EU-finance, healthcare) in canary slices unless compliance sign-off present.

Experiment design (A/B considerations)
- If running true A/B: block randomization at routing layer with sticky assignment for 72 hours to capture downstream effects (session-level stickiness).
- Track both intent-level metrics (task success, completion rate) and economic metrics (tokens per session, total cost).
- Pre-calc minimum detectable effect (MDE) for primary business metric. If MDE > expected, treat as exploratory canary not an A/B.

Rollback and fast fail mechanics
- Immediate rollback options (ordered by speed):
  - Route-level disable via console (fastest) -> revert to previous model variant.
  - Emergency config toggle (rate-limit canary to 0.1%).
  - Autoscaler drain with graceful session reassign.
- Post-rollback steps: open retro ticket (prefix RL-ROLLBACK-YYYYMMDD), collect logs and sample payloads for triage, schedule hotfix (if needed).

Operational play checklist (steward one-pager)
- Pre-activation: confirm dashboards, synth tests green, stakeholders pinged.
- At each phase: tick PhaseA/B/C in sheet, attach sampled 20 responses, confirm human review complete.
- If automated trigger fires: notify oncall, pause rollout, and start rollback procedure.
- Post-activation: submit 24h audit and schedule postmortem if any trigger fired.

Edge cases and unusual failure modes (quick notes)
- Latency oscillation due to batch-sizing interaction: watch token-size distributions; if median input length increases, batching may change and p95 can drift.
- Telemetry lag: don't escalate on a single delayed datapoint; require 3-minute consecutive window for automated triggers.
- Data residency/regulatory slip: if canary unintentionally routes to a region without DPA, immediate halt and legal notification.

Communication script templates (steward to stakeholders)
- Initial post (T-1): "Heads up — rolling new model variant to 0.1% at 14:00 PT. Steward: Aisha P. Rollback plan: console toggle -> old-variant. Watch: p95 latency, 5xx, safety-tag rate. Link: <dashboard>"
- Escalation post: "Escalation: canary triggered p95 latency > threshold at 14:16. Holding traffic at 0.1% and initiating rollback. Assignee: SRE oncall. Ticket: RL-ROLLBACK-20260215-01"

Open questions / items to surface in next sync
- Should we hard-enforce a minimum sample size for human review per phase? (current sketch: 20)
- How quickly can the console disable route-level traffic across Dedicated vs Hosted? (ops capability refinement)
- Add a preflight that simulates cost buckets to detect runaway token cost early.

Next steps (action items)
- Marcus L: prototype a "steward checklist" template in Google Sheets; due 2026-02-20.
- Diego A: add automated synthetic prompt suite to CI for canary routes; due 2026-02-25.
- Renee C: align legal on regional cohort gating; setup 30m sync by 2026-02-22.

Notes-to-self (raw)
- Keep the rhythm light: too many gates means slow rollouts. But missing gates is risky. Need a guardrail list that is terse and machine-enforceable.
- Consider a small "canary mode" flag that disables expensive kernels when triggered to avoid cost-blowouts while keeping feature live.
- Draft a short one-page cheat sheet for oncall with exact console steps for rollback + contact tree.

End of sketch — dump this into the rollout workspace and iterate.
